To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the doping of borons with transition metals (Al, Cu, Sc) or main group elements (Li, Mg) leads to a significant increase of hardness, (ii) the hardness of doped boron increases with the dopant concentration, (iii) the doping of B with transition metals leads to the stabilization of the b rhombohidal polymorph, (iv) the doping of b boron is a promising route for the synthesis of superhard materials, (v

the doping of b by a transition metal M enhances its mechanical properties, in particular its hardness and its elastic modulus, in a way that depends on the concentration of dopant and on its chemical nature.

(1) boron is a promising material for ultrahard applications, (2) the doping of borons with transition metals enhances its hardness, (3) the hardness enhancement can be explained by a model based on the electronic structure of the dopants and (4) the hardness enhancement is accompanied by a significant increase of the bulk modulus and Young's modulus.

the search for new superhard materials, which could be of great interest in industry.
the synthesis of ultrahard materials and the study of their properties.
